newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities steady to higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities were steady to higher on Monday in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.
"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields and bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months was unchanged from last Friday's yield of 2.93/2.88 percent but one-year closed at a yield of 2.75/2.70 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.73/2.68 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 was unchanged from last close of S$98.53/98.58.
May 2002 ended at S$99.38/99.43 against last Friday's close of S$99.33/99.38 and June 2003 at S$94.39/94.44 versus S$94.34/94.44.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-5/8 3-1/2 percent from last Friday's 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent.
